title: Association, aggregation, and composition
answer: Association is the broad relationship where one object knows about or works with another. Aggregation is a weaker whole-part relationship in which the part can exist independently of the whole. Composition is a stronger ownership relationship where the whole controls the part's lifecycle or representation. In Java these are design meanings rather than separate language keywords. AeroTopo's Product owning an immutable copied list of tile IDs is composition-like ownership of its internal representation; a temporary model can illustrate weaker association and aggregation relationships explicitly.

steps.question: AeroTopo's Product constructor copies the supplied tile list with `List. copyOf`, then keeps that private immutable representation as part of the product. Why does copying and owning the internal collection create stronger whole-part ownership than merely remembering an externally managed collection reference?
